summary: All four Phase-0 defects closed, with executable evidence. Important correction to the task premise: items 1, 2 and 4 had ALREADY been applied to the working tree by the earlier verifier pass (all three repos have zero commits — everything is untracked working tree). But item 1's applied fix WAS BROKEN, and I proved it empirically rather than reading it: the gate `CN_KEYS=$(jq '[paths(scalars)]|length' lang/cn.json); if [ "$CN_KEYS" -eq 0 ]` lets a 0-byte and a whitespace-only cn.json SHIP (measured rc=0), because jq treats empty/whitespace input as zero input values (exits 0, prints nothing), so CN_KEYS="", `[ "" -eq 0 ]` returns 2 with `integer expression expected`, and `set -e` is explicitly exempt for a command used as an `if` condition — the else branch runs and the release proceeds. It also shipped `{"a":""}` and `{"a":"   "}`. Only the literal `{}` case was caught. Replaced with a three-part gate (non-zero-byte, `jq -e 'type=="object"'`, at least one non-blank string leaf) and extended the same payload check to modules 2/3, whose `find|wc -l` counted files rather than content. Item 2's workflow guard and register.js comments were present and every Babele citation re-derived and confirmed; the missing piece was the standing QA check, now added to validate_skeleton.py (recursive over all three compendium/cn) together with anti-regression assertions that all three release.yml keep both gates and that the payload gate cannot degrade back to the broken form. Item 3's README note existed but the README CONTRADICTED ITSELF 90 lines later ("我们会把它显式写成英文串" for EVCriticalInjuries) — fixed, and the whole rule rewritten as an (A) shadow / (B) write-nothing table with the 14 orphan keys and the single JSON null re-derived from the installed system. lang_keep_english.json was a bare JSON array with nowhere to put a header, so it is now an object with a 92-line _README plus two tables, and all three QA consumers were updated with a shape-tolerant loader that hard-fails rather than silently returning key names. Item 4 confirmed landed and byte-matching core. Every check run: validate_skeleton.py passes; 27/27 workflow run-blocks pass `bash -n` and all three YAML parse; 25+12 executed gate cases match expectation with 0 mismatches; the gate_fixtures harness still shows GOOD clean and all 30 mutants tripping exactly their own gate.

files_written.what: Replaced the broken 'Verify there is actually something to ship' gate with a three-part fail-closed gate (test -s; jq -e 'type == "object"'; count of non-blank string leaves via `[paths(scalars) as $p | getpath($p) | strings | select(test("[^[:space:]]"))] | length`), with the measured jq/set -e failure mode recorded inline. Also corrected the zip-exclusion comment describing lang_keep_english.json.

Extended the existing file-count gate with a per-file payload check (non-zero-byte + JSON object + >=1 non-blank string leaf), and replaced `for f in $(find …)` with a `while IFS= read -r f … done < <(find …)` loop so a filename containing a space cannot be word-split into bogus paths.
Same payload check and word-splitting fix as module 2.

Added the standing QA guard for item 2: an os.walk over each repo's compendium/cn that FAILs on `mappings.json` or `mapping.json` at any depth, with the source citations for why those two names are reserved. Added four anti-regression assertions per repo: both gate steps must be present by name, and the payload gate must still contain `jq -e 'type == "object"'`, `select(test("[^[:space:]]"))` and a `[ ! -s ` zero-byte check.

Restructured from a bare 10-element JSON array to {_README (92 lines), keep_english (9 keys), never_write (1 key + reason)}. The header documents the write-but-never-delete rule with source lines, the (A) shadow vs (B) write-nothing split, the two actor.mjs lookup traps, the 14 dead orphan keys, and the file's own format contract. ALIENRPG.EVCriticalInjuries moved from the keep list into never_write.

decisions.decision: Treated the task premise 'none has been fixed yet' as wrong and verified before acting
decisions.reason: Items 1, 2 and 4 were already present in the working tree (the earlier verifier's fixes_applied list confirms it; all three repos have zero commits, so nothing is tracked). Blindly re-applying them would have duplicated steps. Verifying instead is what exposed that item 1's applied gate did not actually work.

decisions.decision: Chose `jq -e 'type == "object"'` as the parse/shape check rather than `jq . >/dev/null`
decisions.reason: Measured exit codes distinguish every bad shape and none of them is 0: empty file → 4, whitespace-only → 4, top-level array or null → 1, syntax error → 5. A bare `jq .` returns 0 on empty input, which is the exact hole that broke the original gate.

decisions.decision: Counted non-blank STRING leaves rather than all scalar leaves
decisions.reason: The task asked the gate to fail on an empty/whitespace payload, not merely a missing file. `{"a":""}` and `{"a":"   "}` pass a raw leaf count but ship a no-op module. Verified CJK counts as non-blank under `test("[^[:space:]]")`.

decisions.decision: Used the POSIX class `[^[:space:]]` instead of `\S`
decisions.reason: Avoids backslash-escape mangling across the YAML block scalar / shell / jq string layers — a `\S` variant failed to compile in testing. `[[:space:]]` needs no escapes at any layer.

decisions.decision: Extended the payload check to modules 2 and 3 as well
decisions.reason: Their gate counted .json files, so a 0-byte or `{}` pack file satisfied it. The task's stated criterion — 'not merely on a missing file' — applies identically there, and leaving the asymmetry in place recreates the exact class of defect being closed.

decisions.decision: Put the standing reserved-filename QA check in validate_skeleton.py and made it recursive, while the release-time guard stays at -maxdepth 1
decisions.reason: translation-source.js:83-95 calls FilePicker.browse, which is not recursive, so depth 1 is the real runtime blast radius. The QA walk goes deeper as defence-in-depth against a future refactor that registers a subdirectory; costing nothing today.

decisions.decision: Added anti-regression assertions on the workflows to validate_skeleton.py
decisions.reason: The whole defect was an asymmetry between three near-identical files. A named-step check plus three substring checks on the payload judgement make both the omission and a silent degradation back to the broken jq form fail the standing QA run rather than waiting for a tag.

decisions.decision: Reshaped lang_keep_english.json into an object with a _README and updated all three consumers, rather than leaving a bare array
decisions.reason: A JSON array has nowhere to put the header the task asked for. The risk is that `set(json.load(f))` silently yields key names instead of keys, so the loader accepts both shapes and raises on anything else — the failure mode had to be loud, not an empty whitelist.

decisions.decision: Split the whitelist into keep_english and never_write instead of one flat list
decisions.reason: The two cases are genuinely different and the difference is load-bearing. ALIENRPG.None/OneRound/OneTurn/OneShift/OneDay have real Chinese values upstream, so they MUST be shadowed with English or healTime silently falls to 0. EVCriticalInjuries is JSON null, which localize() already rejects, so writing anything only creates a frozen copy that goes stale if upstream renames the table.

decisions.decision: Fixed the README's self-contradiction rather than only adding new text
decisions.reason: README:106-111 stated the write-nothing rule and README:198-200 stated the opposite for the very key the rule was about. Adding more documentation on top of a live contradiction would have left the wrong instruction in place at the point a maintainer actually reads it.

decisions.decision: Replaced `for f in $(find …)` with a while-read loop in modules 2/3
decisions.reason: A translation filename containing a space would have been word-split into two nonexistent paths and misreported as 'not a JSON object'. Verified with an explicit 'filename WITH A SPACE' fixture in both the good and empty cases.

decisions.decision: Downloaded a pinned jq 1.7.1 binary into the scratchpad rather than reasoning about jq semantics on paper
decisions.reason: The entire item-1 defect lives in undocumented jq exit-code and empty-input behaviour. It is exactly the kind of claim that must be measured; reading the snippet would have concluded the gate was fine.
